contexts.japanese: この矛盾。両立する善意と悪意こそが、人を人たらしめる聖杯だ。
contexts.english: That contradiction, that coexistence of good and evil is a Holy Grail which makes people human.

counterexamples.description: Entity's own judgment stays unknown.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Even if actions evil, people do not yet know its own opinion.
counterexamples.explanation: Entity's own judgment stays unknown.

contexts.japanese: だが—その行為が悪だとしても、アレ本人がそれをどう思うかはまだ判るまい」
contexts.english: However...even if its actions are evil, we do not know what it personally thinks of them."

counterexamples.description: Lamenting existence makes it evil within his framework.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei conditionally calls it evil if it has humanlike will and regrets existence.
counterexamples.explanation: Lamenting existence makes it evil within his framework.

contexts.japanese: もしアレに人に近い意思があり、自らの存在を嘆くのであれば、それは悪だろう。
contexts.english: If it has a human-like will and laments its own existence, that would make it evil.

counterexamples.description: Forgiveness question after total loss retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He asks whether lone survivor after destroying everything can forgive itself.
counterexamples.explanation: Forgiveness question after total loss retained.

contexts.japanese: 「何もかも無くし何もかも壊したあと、ただ一人残ったモノが、果たして自身を許せるのか。
contexts.english: "Once it loses everything, breaks everything, and is all alone, will it forgive itself?

counterexamples.description: Father-killing and Sakura-preservation claim retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei explicitly attributes both acts to desire for answer he cannot give himself.
counterexamples.explanation: Father-killing and Sakura-preservation claim retained.

contexts.japanese: その為におまえの父を殺し、その為に間桐桜を生かした。私では答えは出せない。故に、答えを出せるモノの誕生を願った」
contexts.english: That is why I killed your father and prolonged Sakura Matou's life. I cannot provide the answer, so I wished for the birth of something which can."

counterexamples.description: Shirou understands use of Sakura despite distant goal.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He cannot grasp wish fully but understands Sakura was used for it.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou understands use of Sakura despite distant goal.

contexts.japanese: こいつは—そんな事の為に、桜を。
contexts.english: He used Sakura for a wish like that.

counterexamples.description: Unexpected liking remains tentative.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He thinks he apparently liked Kirei.
counterexamples.explanation: Unexpected liking remains tentative.

contexts.japanese: どうも俺は、言峰綺礼という男が好きだったらしい。
contexts.english: But I think I liked Kirei Kotomine.

counterexamples.description: Both regard themselves as sinners.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou recognizes their shared self-condemnation.
counterexamples.explanation: Both regard themselves as sinners.

contexts.japanese: 共に自身を罪人と思い。
contexts.english: We both think of ourselves as sinners.

counterexamples.description: Impending death is not sole cause of persistence.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei does not stand fast only to obtain wish at life's end.
counterexamples.explanation: Impending death is not sole cause of persistence.

contexts.japanese: ヤツは死に行く体だから、最後に望みを叶えようとしているんじゃない。
contexts.english: It isn't because he's about to die and wants to see his wish come true.

counterexamples.description: Never another path retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei has walked no other life path.
counterexamples.explanation: Never another path retained.

contexts.japanese: 今までそれ以外の道を歩かなかった。
contexts.english: He's never walked any other path.

counterexamples.description: Envy of others explicitly retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei says he envies them.
counterexamples.explanation: Envy of others explicitly retained.

contexts.japanese: 「—私は、おまえたちを羨んでいる。
contexts.english: "...I envy you all.

counterexamples.description: Their happiness gave him no joy.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Recalled split thought says he could not feel their happiness as happiness.
counterexamples.explanation: Their happiness gave him no joy.

contexts.japanese: “—私には、幸福と感じられなかった”
contexts.english: "...never gave me any joy."

contexts.japanese: “おまえたちが幸福と感じるものが—”
contexts.english: "The things which make you feel happiness..."

counterexamples.description: No happiness attained despite repeated seeking.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He sought and obtained no happiness.
counterexamples.explanation: No happiness attained despite repeated seeking.

contexts.japanese: 求めて求めて、何一つ幸福を得られなかった。
contexts.english: He searched and searched, but never gained even one bit of happiness.

counterexamples.description: No magical battle.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Narration denies magecraft battle here.
counterexamples.explanation: No magical battle.

contexts.japanese: 魔術戦になどなる訳がない。
contexts.english: This won't be a battle of magecraft.

counterexamples.description: Counter misses and own chest struck.
counterexamples.sourceReading: His right fist misses; impact is received in his chest.
counterexamples.explanation: Counter misses and own chest struck.

contexts.japanese: だが、突き出した右拳は宙を切り、衝撃を受けたのはこちらの胸元。
contexts.english: But my right fist cuts through empty air, and it's my chest that takes an impact.

counterexamples.description: Opponent folds left and strikes abdomen.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei lowers tall body to boy's left and punches stomach.
counterexamples.explanation: Opponent folds left and strikes abdomen.

contexts.japanese: 長身を折り畳むよう俺の左横に屈み、拳で腹を殴りつけ、
contexts.english: He bends his tall body to my left flank, drives a fist into my stomach,

counterexamples.description: Organ-destroying power remains counterfactual.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Even second punch had power to destroy organs.
counterexamples.explanation: Organ-destroying power remains counterfactual.

contexts.japanese: いや、それを言うなら腹を叩いた二撃目ですら、内臓を破壊する威力があった。
contexts.english: No, if we're going with that, even the second blow to my stomach would have destroyed my organs.

counterexamples.description: Chinese martial arts, unnamed school.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou identifies Chinese martial arts used by priest.
counterexamples.explanation: Chinese martial arts, unnamed school.

contexts.japanese: 「神父のクセに、中国拳法、なんて」
contexts.english: "You're a priest who uses Chinese martial arts...?"

counterexamples.description: Teacher's forms and adequacy against dying man.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei calls forms imitation, sufficient against a dying foe.
counterexamples.explanation: Teacher's forms and adequacy against dying man.

contexts.japanese: 「そうでもない。私のコレは真似事だ。師の套路を真似ただけの、内に何も宿らぬ物だが—死に損ないの相手には十分のようだ」
contexts.english: "Not quite. I simply imitate my teacher's taolu. My moves lack internal power...but it is sufficient against a dying man."

counterexamples.description: Striking blade body costs attacker.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Bloody hand is price of attacking bundle of blades barehanded.
counterexamples.explanation: Striking blade body costs attacker.

contexts.japanese: 刃の塊を素手で砕こうとした代償だった。
contexts.english: what he gets for hitting a bundle of blades.

counterexamples.description: Lethal thorns will not stop him.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei will continue even against death-thorn body.
counterexamples.explanation: Lethal thorns will not stop him.

contexts.japanese: あいつは、たとえ相手が死の棘だろうと手を止める事はしない。
contexts.english: He won't stop even if his opponent is covered with lethal thorns.

counterexamples.description: Battle wagers own selves.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He frames battle as wagering selves rather than just outside threat.
counterexamples.explanation: Battle wagers own selves.

contexts.japanese: 「外敵との戦いではなく、自身を賭ける戦いという事だ—！」
contexts.english: "A battle not against an outside threat, but which wagers our very selves on the outcome!"

counterexamples.description: Hourglass vessel breaks before sand empties.
counterexamples.sourceReading: At current rate body-clock vessel shatters before life-time runs out.
counterexamples.explanation: Hourglass vessel breaks before sand empties.

contexts.japanese: このままでいけば、砂時計が空っぽになる前に砂時計ごと破壊される。
contexts.english: At this rate, my hourglass will shatter before it even runs out.

counterexamples.description: Cave-in excluded from attention.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He no longer perceives collapse and falling rubble.
counterexamples.explanation: Cave-in excluded from attention.

contexts.japanese: 止まない落盤の音も、雨のように降り注ぐ土塊も目に入らない。
contexts.english: I don't perceive the sounds of the collapsing cave and the rain of rubble at all.

counterexamples.description: Immediate opponent is target.
counterexamples.sourceReading: What he must defeat is in front of him.
counterexamples.explanation: Immediate opponent is target.

contexts.japanese: 倒すべきモノは目の前にいる。
contexts.english: The thing I need to beat is right in front of me.

counterexamples.description: Kirei hypothetical voice retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Rin imagines Kirei would call her agent of God.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei hypothetical voice retained.

contexts.japanese: 「……まいった。綺礼がいたら、神の代行者とか言うんだろうな……」
contexts.english: "...Oh, crap. If Kirei was here, he'd probably call her an agent of God...."

counterexamples.description: Kirei death is speculative.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Rin says it sounds like Sakura killed Kirei.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei death is speculative.

contexts.japanese: 「……ふうん。そのわりにはご機嫌じゃない。臓硯を殺してアサシンも殺して、その分じゃ綺礼もアンタに殺されたと見るべきね。
contexts.english: "Oh, yeah? You seem to be in a pretty good mood despite everything. You killed Zouken, killed Assassin, and it sounds like you even killed Kirei.

counterexamples.description: Internal destruction bypasses altered exterior.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Palm blow targets interior rather than surface.
counterexamples.explanation: Internal destruction bypasses altered exterior.

contexts.japanese: 外側ではなく内側の破壊を旨とした一撃は、容赦なく衝撃を通してくる。
contexts.english: His attack, aimed at doing internal rather than external damage, ruthlessly sends shockwaves through me.

counterexamples.description: Head strike can end combat in one blow.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Untransformed face/head only vulnerable surface.
counterexamples.explanation: Head strike can end combat in one blow.

contexts.japanese: 頭に直撃されては一撃で終わる。
contexts.english: This could end with a single blow to my head.

counterexamples.description: Kirei endures reciprocal injury with visible pain.
counterexamples.sourceReading: His hand bones break and face twists, continues striking.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei endures reciprocal injury with visible pain.

contexts.japanese: それに耐え、顔を苦悶に歪めながら敵は俺を打ってくる。
contexts.english: He endures it, his face twisted in pain, and continues striking me.

counterexamples.description: Both unable to run retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei too can only walk, both nearing disappearance.
counterexamples.explanation: Both unable to run retained.

contexts.japanese: ……もう走る事もできないのは敵も同じ。
contexts.english: ...He can't run anymore, either.

counterexamples.description: Counted barrage reaches seven.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Two through seven after first blow, then counter.
counterexamples.explanation: Counted barrage reaches seven.

contexts.japanese: 七撃—！
contexts.english: Seven blows...!

counterexamples.description: Kirei's superior strength retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Many times stronger means cannot easily hit him.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei's superior strength retained.

contexts.japanese: ちくしょう、そうだよ、そう簡単に殴らせてなんてくれねえよ、あいつの方が何倍も強いんだから、
contexts.english: Damn it, that's right, he won't let me hit him that easily, and he's many times stronger than me...

counterexamples.description: Convenient skill reversal rejected.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Difference of ability cannot be overturned.
counterexamples.explanation: Convenient skill reversal rejected.

contexts.japanese: 実力差は覆らない。
contexts.english: I can't overcome the difference in fighting strength.

counterexamples.description: Earlier forest death timing retained as inference.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei reached dying condition slightly earlier in forest.
counterexamples.explanation: Earlier forest death timing retained as inference.

contexts.japanese: あの森で死に体になったのは、わずかに、この男の方が早かったのか。
contexts.english: He must have started dying just slightly before me in the forest.

counterexamples.description: Victory concession and only seconds remaining retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei concedes, urges goal with uncertain brief bodily duration.
counterexamples.explanation: Victory concession and only seconds remaining retained.

contexts.japanese: 「おまえの勝ちだ衛宮士郎。その体で何秒保つかは知らんが、目的があるのなら急ぐがいい」
contexts.english: "You win, Shirou Emiya. I don't know how many more seconds your body will last, but hurry to your goal if you have one."

counterexamples.description: Enemy remains detestable at final moment.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Unchanged even dying, continues as hated enemy.
counterexamples.explanation: Enemy remains detestable at final moment.

contexts.japanese: 崩れていくこの瞬間さえ、いけすかない俺の敵であり続ける。
contexts.english: He's still my detestable enemy, even as he crumbles away.

counterexamples.description: Final expression uncertain with useless vision.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Whether he smiled cannot be determined by failing eyes.
counterexamples.explanation: Final expression uncertain with useless vision.

contexts.japanese: 最期に男は笑ったのか。
contexts.english: Did he laugh at the end?

contexts.japanese: スクラップ寸前の俺の眼は用を成さず、
contexts.english: My nearly scrap metal eyes are useless.

counterexamples.description: Expected Kirei recognition is boy inference.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Should notice bodily abnormality from oversight/prior-war survival/treatment.
counterexamples.explanation: Expected Kirei recognition is boy inference.

contexts.japanese: なら、桜の体の異状に気がついて然るべきだろう……！
contexts.english: Then he definitely would have noticed what was wrong with Sakura...!

counterexamples.description: Worm reduction doesn't disable other monitoring.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Priest reduced worms, merely insurance; different means tracks heartbeat.
counterexamples.explanation: Worm reduction doesn't disable other monitoring.

contexts.japanese: あの神父の治療で体内の刻印虫が減っていようと関係ない。
contexts.english: It doesn't matter that the priest reduced the number of worms in my body.

contexts.japanese: ……だって、あんなものはただの保険だ。
contexts.english: ...They were just insurance.

contexts.japanese: いまのわたしの体調。心拍音すら聴いている。
contexts.english: Of knowing my physical condition. He's even listening to my heartbeat.

counterexamples.description: Kirei recognized black Grail during treatment.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Opened body and saw adjusted vessel.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei recognized black Grail during treatment.

contexts.japanese: 「当然だ。あの娘の体を開いて見たのだからな。アレが間桐臓硯によって調整された、黒い聖杯だという事は判っていた」
contexts.english: "Of course. I saw what was inside her when I opened her up. It was apparent that she was a dark Holy Grail fashioned by Zouken Matou."

counterexamples.description: Effort for extra life beyond Sakura herself.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Wouldn't act so much if only Sakura dying.
counterexamples.explanation: Effort for extra life beyond Sakura herself.

contexts.japanese: 人間は死ぬものだ。間桐桜が死ぬというのならそれも道理だろう。死にゆくものが彼女だけならば、私もあそこまで手は尽くさなかった」
contexts.english: All humans die, and that applies to Sakura Matou as well. If her life had been the only one in danger, I never would have gone to such lengths."

counterexamples.description: Different rescue motives explicit.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Protected mother to save gestating darkness versus boy saving girl.
counterexamples.explanation: Different rescue motives explicit.

contexts.japanese: 私は間桐桜が孕んだ闇を救う為、彼女を救った。
contexts.english: I saved her to save the darkness she was pregnant with.

counterexamples.description: Gratitude bounded to outcome.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Whatever motive treatment helped and full crest spent; should thank result.
counterexamples.explanation: Gratitude bounded to outcome.

contexts.japanese: その結果だけは、感謝するべき事だろう。
contexts.english: I should be grateful for the outcome.

counterexamples.description: Not lie yet not whole truth.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Zouken explanation partial, power originally colorless.
counterexamples.explanation: Not lie yet not whole truth.

contexts.japanese: 「そうだな。臓硯の説明に嘘はなかろう。だが真実も語ってはいない。
contexts.english: "Yes. Zouken's explanation was not false. But he also has not told you the entire truth.

counterexamples.description: Directionless power disperses rather than attacks.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Colorless lacks purpose, not self-attacks.
counterexamples.explanation: Directionless power disperses rather than attacks.

contexts.japanese: 無色である以上、自分から人を襲う、などという事はない。目的のない力は、目的のないまま霧散するものだろう」
contexts.english: Because it lacks any color or will, it would never do anything such as attacking people on its own. Power without direction simply disperses without anything to focus it."

counterexamples.description: Contamination doesn't remove wish function.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Still wish engine, result ethics distorted.
counterexamples.explanation: Contamination doesn't remove wish function.

contexts.japanese: 願望機としての機能は損なわれていない。
contexts.english: It has not lost its function as a wish-granter.

counterexamples.description: Servant drenching and fire history retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Mud drenches Kirei's servant and burns town/kills.
counterexamples.explanation: Servant drenching and fire history retained.

contexts.japanese: 「その結果は言うまでもない。私のサーヴァントは汚染された聖杯の中身を浴び、聖杯から漏れた泥は街を燃やし、人を殺めた。
contexts.english: "The result was obvious. My Servant was bathed in the tainted contents of the Holy Grail, and the mud that spilled out of the Grail set fire to the town, killing many people.

counterexamples.description: Gate/opening dual layer retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Grail gate with hole/opening ruby.
counterexamples.explanation: Gate/opening dual layer retained.

contexts.japanese: 「そう、聖杯という門だ。
contexts.english: "The opening, the gate which we call the Holy Grail.

counterexamples.description: Third-ritual origin remains likely.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Most likely forbidden Einzbern summoning caused impurity.
counterexamples.explanation: Third-ritual origin remains likely.

contexts.japanese: 「おそらくな。三度目の儀式のおり、アインツベルンは喚んではならぬモノを召喚した。その結果、彼らが用意した聖杯戦争という儀式に不純物が混入した。
contexts.english: "Most likely. During the third ritual, the Einzberns summoned something forbidden. In doing so, they introduced an impurity into their Holy Grail.

counterexamples.description: Fifty-year waiting with failed emergence.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Third to fourth50years awaiting birth, couldn't emerge.
counterexamples.explanation: Fifty-year waiting with failed emergence.

contexts.japanese: 三度目から四度目の間。五十年の歳月をかけて聖杯の中で出産を待った不純物は、しかし外界に出る事は叶わなかった」
contexts.english: For the fifty years between the third and fourth wars, that impurity awaited its birth in the Holy Grail. But it was never allowed to emerge."

counterexamples.description: Incomplete Grail nevertheless gate opens then destroyed.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Saber/Archer remain, expired ritual incomplete; gate promptly destroyed.
counterexamples.explanation: Incomplete Grail nevertheless gate opens then destroyed.

contexts.japanese: 前回はセイバーとアーチャーが残ったまま期限を迎え、聖杯は完成しなかった。門こそ開いたものの、それは即座に切嗣によって破壊された」
contexts.english: While it was still incomplete, time ran out while Saber and Archer were still intact. Then, Kiritsugu destroyed the gate as soon as it opened."

counterexamples.description: Not person, directed pure power.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Tainted still power vortex with orientation.
counterexamples.explanation: Not person, directed pure power.

contexts.japanese: 黒く染まろうと聖杯の中身は純粋な“力”の渦にすぎない。中にあるものは方向性を持った魔力だ。
contexts.english: The contents of the Holy Grail are still pure power, even if it is tainted. It is magical energy with an orientation.

counterexamples.description: Still unborn and manifestation depends on Sakura.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Unborn child cannot cast shadow without her.
counterexamples.explanation: Still unborn and manifestation depends on Sakura.

contexts.japanese: 「それが聖杯の中にいる現象—夜に徘徊する影の本体だ。まだ生まれておらず、間桐桜がいなければ影さえ落とせない“出産予定児”にすぎないが」
contexts.english: "That is the identity of the phenomenon within the Holy Grail, the Shadow, which roams at night. It is an unborn fetus which would not even cast a shadow if not for Sakura Matou."

counterexamples.description: Proper-vessel delivery contrasted with special Sakura.
counterexamples.sourceReading: If normal correct Grail body would release entity; she special.
counterexamples.explanation: Proper-vessel delivery contrasted with special Sakura.

contexts.japanese: 「いいや。間桐桜が正しく作られた聖杯ならば、たしかに彼女の肉体からソレは現れるだろう。
contexts.english: "No, no. If Sakura Matou had been a properly constructed Holy Grail, her body would give birth to it.

counterexamples.description: Power inheritance permits existence without ordinary flesh.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Give own force to Sakura to become from nothing.
counterexamples.explanation: Power inheritance permits existence without ordinary flesh.

contexts.japanese: 「己が誕生。無から有に至るため、彼女に自身の力を受け渡す事で、この世に存在まれようとしているのだ。
contexts.english: "In passing its own power to Sakura, it is trying to exist in this world. It is attempting to make its own birth happen, to become something from nothing.

counterexamples.description: Shadow already Sakura, not only spill.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Explicitly she herself now shadow.
counterexamples.explanation: Shadow already Sakura, not only spill.

contexts.japanese: アレは既に間桐桜そのものだ。
contexts.english: It is already Sakura Matou herself.

counterexamples.description: Alternative amorphous vessels remain hypothetical.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Gold/bronze alternatives would lack form, might proliferate flesh.
counterexamples.explanation: Alternative amorphous vessels remain hypothetical.

contexts.japanese: 通常の聖杯……アインツベルン製の黄金や、魔術師の肉体を使った青銅の聖杯ならば象にはならず、不確かなカタチになっていただろう。なにしろ質量を持つほどの呪いだ。場合によっては、ただ増殖するだけの肉の塊になるやもしれん」
contexts.english: With a normal Holy Grail, such as one made out of the Einzberns' gold or a bronze chalice using a mage's body, it would have remained amorphous and indefinite. It is a bundle of curses potent enough to have actual mass. Under some circumstances, it might have multiplied into a great lump of flesh."

counterexamples.description: Rational resistance limits entity via her command.
counterexamples.sourceReading: While closes gate, resides within cannot emerge fully.
counterexamples.explanation: Rational resistance limits entity via her command.

contexts.japanese: いかに呪いが間桐桜を汚染しようと、命令権は彼女にある。彼女が聖杯として門を閉じようとするかぎり、中のモノは間桐桜に宿るだけで、完全には外に出られない」
contexts.english: No matter how tainted she is by the curse, she is in command. As long as she tries to keep the gate closed, it will continue to stay within her and cannot completely emerge."

counterexamples.description: Master–Servant analogy explicit.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Curse servant can't overturn Sakura mastery.
counterexamples.explanation: Master–Servant analogy explicit.

contexts.japanese: 「マスターとサーヴァントの関係と同じだ。
contexts.english: "It is like the relationship between Master and Servant.

counterexamples.description: Existing killings counter unborn-defense argument.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Boy says actual demon already killing.
counterexamples.explanation: Existing killings counter unborn-defense argument.

contexts.japanese: 「当然だろう……！　あの影は悪魔だ。今だって際限なく人を殺しまくる悪魔じゃないか……！」
contexts.english: "Obviously! That Shadow is a demon. It's a demon that goes around killing people left and right!"

counterexamples.description: Different born thing is Kirei's distinction.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Current shadow modeled on host, future something different.
counterexamples.explanation: Different born thing is Kirei's distinction.

contexts.japanese: 「それが間違いだ。あの影は間桐桜という依り代から象った影にすぎん。聖杯より生まれ出ようとするものはアレとは違う何かだ。
contexts.english: "You are mistaken. The Shadow you speak of is a shade modeled after its host, Sakura Matou. It is a separate entity from the thing which wishes to be born from the Holy Grail.

counterexamples.description: Silence explicitly not accepting argument.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Not agreeing on transformation, accusation won't save girl.
counterexamples.explanation: Silence explicitly not accepting argument.

contexts.japanese: 桜を“聖杯の中身”に変貌させる……いや、そうなる事を否定しない、という言峰の言い分を許したワケじゃない。
contexts.english: I don't accept Kotomine's argument to turn Sakura into the "contents of the Holy Grail"... or rather, that he refuses to stop it from happening.

contexts.japanese: ただ、今はこいつを糾弾したところで何が変わるワケでもなく、桜が助かるワケでもない。
contexts.english: But attacking him for what he just said won't change anything, and it won't help Sakura.

counterexamples.description: Opponent but neither Grail power nor Sakura's life sought.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He contrasts own goal with Zouken.
counterexamples.explanation: Opponent but neither Grail power nor Sakura's life sought.

contexts.japanese: 「無論だ。だが、私は間桐桜の命が欲しい訳ではないし、間桐臓硯のように聖杯の力が欲しい訳でもない。
contexts.english: "Of course. However, I do not want to take her life, nor do I desire the Holy Grail's power as Zouken Matou does.

counterexamples.description: Prebirth refusal remains respected.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Mother rejects before birth, honors her will.
counterexamples.explanation: Prebirth refusal remains respected.

contexts.japanese: 聖杯の中にあるモノ。それが生命として誕生した時のみ、ソレを擁護する。出産の前に間桐桜が子を拒むのであらば、そちらの意思を尊重しよう」
contexts.english: I protect that which is within the Holy Grail, so that it may be born. If its mother rejects her child before it is born, then I will respect her wishes."

counterexamples.description: No intended forced transformation retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Boy judges sincere observer rather than forced changer.
counterexamples.explanation: No intended forced transformation retained.

contexts.japanese: 桜に無理強いさせて“変貌”させる気などない。
contexts.english: He doesn't intend to force Sakura's transformation.

counterexamples.description: Nonaggression conditional on staying observer.
counterexamples.sourceReading: If only watching won't attack, debt from treatment.
counterexamples.explanation: Nonaggression conditional on staying observer.

contexts.japanese: 「……わかった。アンタが傍観に徹するんなら俺も手は出さない。理由はどうあれ、アンタは桜を助けてくれた。
contexts.english: "...All right. If you're set on watching from the sidelines, then I won't go after you. You did save Sakura, whatever your reasons.

counterexamples.description: Physical concern corrected to mind.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei advises return to protect mental state.
counterexamples.explanation: Physical concern corrected to mind.

contexts.japanese: 桜の体—いや、心を気遣って神父は言う。
contexts.english: The priest says it out of concern for Sakura's physical—no, her mental health.

counterexamples.description: Personality death and narrow resistance hope retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Complete Grail threatens personality; small endurance interval hope.
counterexamples.explanation: Personality death and narrow resistance hope retained.

contexts.japanese: 聖杯として完成すれば、間桐桜という人格は消え去るだろう。だが、聖杯が放つ“力”に彼女の精神が少しでも耐えられるのなら—その僅かな時間が希望になる」
contexts.english: Once she is a complete Holy Grail, Sakura Matou's personality will likely disappear. If her mind can withstand the power of the Holy Grail at all, however...it may buy her a short amount of time."

counterexamples.description: Crest worms and inhabiting thing both purge targets.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kill both using corrupted killing-power itself.
counterexamples.explanation: Crest worms and inhabiting thing both purge targets.

contexts.japanese: 要は力ずくだ。間桐桜を聖杯に仕立て上げる刻印虫も、彼女の肉体を依り代にするモノも、聖杯の力で『殺して』しまえばよい。
contexts.english: It is a brute-force approach. One need merely use the power of the Holy Grail to kill the Crest Worms upon which her Grail was built, and the thing inhabiting her body.

counterexamples.description: Rin synchronization possible but agreement doubtful.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Sister can synchronize/soften backlash, doubtful consent.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin synchronization possible but agreement doubtful.

contexts.japanese: 凛は間桐桜の姉だ。妹の精神に同調し、聖杯からの反動を和らげる事も容易だろう。
contexts.english: Rin is Sakura Matou's older sister. It would be easy for her to synchronize her mind with Sakura's and lessen the feedback from the Holy Grail.

contexts.japanese: もっとも、そんな馬鹿げた賭けに凛が賛同するとは思えないが」
contexts.english: Though, I doubt she would agree to such an absurd course of action."

counterexamples.description: Rescue doesn't erase prior consumed lives.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Even no Grail still killed/eaten; questions defending sinner.
counterexamples.explanation: Rescue doesn't erase prior consumed lives.

contexts.japanese: だが、おまえはそれでいいのかな衛宮士郎。間桐桜が聖杯でなくなったとしても、彼女が既に“人食い”である事に変わりはない。その罪人を、おまえは擁護するというのか？」
contexts.english: But is that something you can accept, Shirou Emiya? Even if she is no longer the Holy Grail, it does not change the fact that she has eaten other people. Can you defend such a sinner?"

counterexamples.description: Ordinary happiness never gives Kirei joy.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Other people's named happiness didn't make him happy.
counterexamples.explanation: Ordinary happiness never gives Kirei joy.

contexts.japanese: 「—いや。おまえたちが幸福と呼ぶものでは、私に喜びを与えなかった」
contexts.english: "...No. The things which you call happiness have never given me any joy."

counterexamples.description: Kiritsugu had and sacrificed what Kirei lacked.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Existing feelings abandoned versus never present.
counterexamples.explanation: Kiritsugu had and sacrificed what Kirei lacked.

contexts.japanese: ヤツは初めからあったモノを切り捨て、私には初めから、切り捨てられるモノがなかった。
contexts.english: He abandoned that which he had from the beginning, while I never had anything to abandon.

counterexamples.description: Why born grievance retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: If never capable of those things why given life.
counterexamples.explanation: Why born grievance retained.

contexts.japanese: 「その違いこそが決定的だった。そう。初めから持ち得ないのなら。何故、私はこの世に生を受けたのか」
contexts.english: "It was a critical difference between us. Yes, if I was never to have such things, then why was I given life in this world?"

counterexamples.description: Narration recognizes genuine anger.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Words contain real feeling boy thought absent.
counterexamples.explanation: Narration recognizes genuine anger.

contexts.japanese: ……ただ、今の言葉には怒りがあった。
contexts.english: But I can feel the anger in his words.

counterexamples.description: Envy tag retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei soliloquy sounds somewhat envious.
counterexamples.explanation: Envy tag retained.

contexts.japanese: どこか羨むように、言峰綺礼は独白した。
contexts.english: Kirei Kotomine thinks out loud, sounding somewhat envious.

counterexamples.description: Zouken occupancy after personality loss threatens rescue.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Empty body taken over then girl unrecoverable.
counterexamples.explanation: Zouken occupancy after personality loss threatens rescue.

contexts.japanese: どのようなカタチであれ間桐桜を救いたいのであらば、間桐臓硯を殺す事だ。ヤツは間桐桜の精神が消え去った後、空になった肉体に乗り移る。そうなっては、間桐桜を取り戻す事もできなくなる」
contexts.english: If you wish to save Sakura Matou in any form, you must kill Zouken Matou. He plans to take over her empty body once her mind is gone. If that happens, it will be impossible to bring her back."

counterexamples.description: Soul anchor and purification alternatives retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Find main body or purify soul for full destruction.
counterexamples.explanation: Soul anchor and purification alternatives retained.

contexts.japanese: 間桐臓硯はある意味不老不死だ。魂を世に留めている手のひらほどの本体を探し出すか、魂そのものを浄化させなければ完全には滅ぼせん」
contexts.english: He is immortal, in a way. He will never completely disappear unless you find the main body which anchors his soul, or cleanse his soul itself."

counterexamples.description: Defeat Zouken then winner/control/purge sequence.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Outlined policy tentative, must gain/control engine.
counterexamples.explanation: Defeat Zouken then winner/control/purge sequence.

contexts.japanese: 間桐臓硯を倒し、間桐桜を勝者にする。その後に現れる聖杯を制御し、間桐桜の身体を洗浄する。方針としてはそんなところか」
contexts.english: Your next steps are to defeat Zouken Matou and make Sakura Matou the victor. Then, control the Holy Grail once it appears and use it to cleanse Sakura Matou's body."

counterexamples.description: Compatibility theory attributed personal opinion.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei labels view personal.
counterexamples.explanation: Compatibility theory attributed personal opinion.

contexts.japanese: 「これは私見だがな。間桐桜の精神は存外に強く、聖杯の“呪い”に適合しすぎている。
contexts.english: "This is only my personal opinion, but Sakura Matou's body is stronger and more suitable to the Holy Grail's curse than expected.

counterexamples.description: Shared prevent-Zouken restriction survives opposed goals.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Above all don't hand girl to Zouken.
counterexamples.explanation: Shared prevent-Zouken restriction survives opposed goals.

contexts.japanese: 「その意気だ。決して、臓硯にだけは手渡すな」
contexts.english: "That's the spirit. Do not, by any means, let her fall into Zouken's hands."

counterexamples.description: Boy's exclusive knowledge assertion remains focalized.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Only he thinks knows prognosis; cannot tell women.
counterexamples.explanation: Boy's exclusive knowledge assertion remains focalized.

contexts.japanese: それを知っているのは俺だけだ。
contexts.english: I'm the only one who knows that.

counterexamples.description: Priest cannot beat Sakura is her own speech.
counterexamples.sourceReading: あの人 follows priest warning and she claims he can't win against her.
counterexamples.explanation: Priest cannot beat Sakura is her own speech.

contexts.japanese: だってあの人、わたしには勝てないもの」
contexts.english: He can't beat me."

counterexamples.description: Kirei warns Shirou no longer has fighting body.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Repeated priestly warning.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei warns Shirou no longer has fighting body.

contexts.japanese: 「忘れるな衛宮士郎。おまえは戦える体ではない」
contexts.english: "Do not forget, Shirou Emiya. You no longer have a body that can fight."

counterexamples.description: Sakura's decline drives Shirou's fighting, which hastens his death.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Causal chain is commitment-mediated.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura's decline drives Shirou's fighting, which hastens his death.

contexts.japanese: いいかね衛宮士郎。おまえも危うい体だが、間桐桜は更に危うい爆弾を抱えている。おまえは戦わなければ無事だが、間桐桜は刻一刻と崩壊している。だからこそおまえは戦いを止められない。戦闘が、自らの死期を早めると承知した上で」
contexts.english: Listen well, Shirou Emiya. Your condition may be precarious, but Sakura Matou carries an even more disastrous bomb. You may be fine as long as you don't fight, but Sakura Matou is falling apart with each passing hour. That is why you cannot stop fighting, even if you know it will hasten your demise."

counterexamples.description: Saving Sakura is framed as self-killing by Kirei.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Provocative conclusion from current injury/commitment.
counterexamples.explanation: Saving Sakura is framed as self-killing by Kirei.

contexts.japanese: 故に—間桐桜を救うという事は、自分を殺すという事だと理解しているな？」
contexts.english: Do you understand that saving Sakura Matou means killing yourself?"

counterexamples.description: Kirei's possible fallibility is imagined, not established.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou says he believes him but asks what if he is wrong.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei's possible fallibility is imagined, not established.

contexts.japanese: あの神父の言葉を信用していない訳じゃないが、あいつにだって間違いはあるだろうし。
contexts.english: It's not that I don't believe what the priest said, but what if he's wrong?

counterexamples.description: Shirou concludes unwrapping will kill him.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The warning is accepted after direct exposure.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou concludes unwrapping will kill him.

contexts.japanese: 解けば死ぬ。
contexts.english: If I take it off, I'll die.

counterexamples.description: Kirei's warning is accepted as true.
counterexamples.sourceReading: This overturns Shirou's preceding fantasy of priestly error.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei's warning is accepted as true.

contexts.japanese: 神父の言葉は真実だ。
contexts.english: The priest was telling the truth.

counterexamples.description: Shirou has heard what happened but refuses to claim lived understanding.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Information and understanding are separated.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou has heard what happened but refuses to claim lived understanding.

contexts.japanese: いや、言峰の口からどんなものだったかはとっくに聞いている。
contexts.english: Though, I've already heard from Kotomine's lips what happened to her.

counterexamples.description: Illya looks away because explanation is difficult.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei then takes over.
counterexamples.explanation: Illya looks away because explanation is difficult.

contexts.japanese: 言いにくそうに視線を逸らす。
contexts.english: She looks away uncomfortably.

counterexamples.description: Illya refuses to leave Shirou alone with Kirei.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She says she will leave with Shirou and challenges the priest's harmlessness.
counterexamples.explanation: Illya refuses to leave Shirou alone with Kirei.

contexts.japanese: 「……ふん、どうだか。わたしはシロウと一緒に外に出るの。アナタが本当に何もしないのなら、わたしがここにいても問題はないでしょう？」
contexts.english: "...Hmph, sure you will. I'm going to leave with Shirou. If you really aren't going to do anything to him, then there shouldn't be a problem if I stay."

counterexamples.description: Kirei says the arm came from Archer by Archer's intent.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Donation and source side are explicit.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei says the arm came from Archer by Archer's intent.

contexts.japanese: 「アーチャーの左腕だ。アーチャー本人の意思を尊重し、彼の遺体からおまえに移植した」
contexts.english: "Archer's left arm. I honored his last wishes and transplanted it from his corpse."

counterexamples.description: Archer disappears only after transplantation is complete.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Independent Action lets him endure until then.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer disappears only after transplantation is complete.

contexts.japanese: 「移植が済んだ後、消滅した。ここに運ばれた時点で死に体だったのだが、よくも終わるまで保ったものだ。アーチャーの持つ単独行動故だろうがな」
contexts.english: "After the transplant, he disappeared. He was already on the verge of death when he brought you here. I'm surprised he lasted so long. It must be thanks to his Independent Action ability."

counterexamples.description: Shirou questions why a vanished Servant's arm remains.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The continuity problem is raised directly.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou questions why a vanished Servant's arm remains.

contexts.japanese: 「……待て。アーチャーは消えたんだろう。なら、あいつの腕が残っているのはおかしくないか」
contexts.english: "...Wait. You said Archer disappeared. Then how is his arm still here?"

counterexamples.description: The arm was detached and connected while Archer remained in the world.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou's circuits and energy sustain it as flesh.
counterexamples.explanation: The arm was detached and connected while Archer remained in the world.

contexts.japanese: 「移植が終わる前に消滅したのなら、その左腕も消えていただろう。だがおまえのソレはアーチャーが現世に留まっているうちに切り離し、おまえの体に植え付けたものだ。衛宮士郎の魔術回路と繋げ、おまえ自身の魔力で現世に受肉させている英霊の肉。
contexts.english: "If he had passed on before the transplant was complete, then the arm would have gone as well. But your new arm was amputated and transplanted while he was still in the mortal world. It is the incarnated flesh of a Heroic Spirit, connected to Shirou Emiya's Magic Circuits and incarnated by your own magical energy.

counterexamples.description: Completed surgery makes the arm Shirou's body before Archer vanishes.
counterexamples.sourceReading: This explains persistence.
counterexamples.explanation: Completed surgery makes the arm Shirou's body before Archer vanishes.

contexts.japanese: ……その手術が成った時点で、ソレはおまえの肉体となった。その後ならばアーチャーが消えようと左腕は残る。その左腕は既におまえの腕なのだからな」
contexts.english: ...It became a part of your body once the surgery was complete. Afterward, Archer disappeared, leaving his left arm behind. It is now your arm."

counterexamples.description: Both Archer and Shirou were near death.
counterexamples.sourceReading: A broken spiritual core and catastrophic tissue loss motivate the operation.
counterexamples.explanation: Both Archer and Shirou were near death.

contexts.japanese: 「そうだ。あのままではおまえもアーチャーも長くはなかった。アーチャーはこの世に留まる霊核を壊されており、おまえも半死半生の手負いで、傷口より生命活動に必要な中身を損ねていた。
contexts.english: "Yes. At the time, neither you nor Archer had much time left to live. Archer's spiritual core keeping him in this world was destroyed, and you were critically wounded, lacking vital life-sustaining tissues.

counterexamples.description: Archer supplies an intact body part so Shirou can live.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Donation is lifesaving rather than power enhancement.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer supplies an intact body part so Shirou can live.

contexts.japanese: 幸い、アーチャーの体に傷は少なかったからな。彼はおまえに唯一無事な肉体を提供する事で、死にゆくおまえを生かしたのだ」
contexts.english: Fortunately, Archer's body was only lightly damaged. He gave you the only unscathed part of his body so that you might live."

counterexamples.description: Illya distinguishes spiritual healing from ordinary bodily medicine.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She recognizes Kirei's genuine skill.
counterexamples.explanation: Illya distinguishes spiritual healing from ordinary bodily medicine.

contexts.japanese: 「繋げるだけなら出来なくもないわ。霊媒の医師は肉体ではなく魂を癒すものだっていうし、そこの神父は見かけによらず本物だったっていう事ね」
contexts.english: "It isn't impossible to connect them. It's said that spiritual healers treat the soul, not the body, and that priest turned out to be a real one, despite all appearances."

counterexamples.description: Kirei says soul restoration is beyond magecraft.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He expected physical success followed by shock death.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei says soul restoration is beyond magecraft.

contexts.japanese: 霊体……魂の蘇生、復元は魔術では扱えない神秘である。故に今回も、形だけ成功した後でショック死すると思ったのだが—」
contexts.english: The resurrection and restoration of spiritual bodies...of souls is a Mystic beyond the scope of magecraft. That is why I expected it to work only in shape, and that you would die of shock afterward..."

counterexamples.description: Kirei knows compatibility exceeds twins but not why.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The explanation remains withheld.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei knows compatibility exceeds twins but not why.

contexts.japanese: 「ほう。まあ、その理由は知らん。私に判るのはおまえたちの相性がよかった、という事だけだ。手術を始めた時は驚いたぞ。双子でもここまで瓜二つではなかろう、とな」
contexts.english: "Oh? Well, I don't know the reason. I just know that you were highly compatible. I was surprised once the operation began. Even identical twins aren't so similar."

counterexamples.description: Kirei predicts adaptation in days and ordinary-life recovery.
counterexamples.sourceReading: This is a prognosis, not current function.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei predicts adaptation in days and ordinary-life recovery.

contexts.japanese: 「無茶を言うな。繋げたばかりではそれが限界だ。数日経てば馴染む。先ほども言ったが、おまえたちの相性は実にいい。この分であれば、通常の生活をこなせるほどには回復しよう」
contexts.english: "Don't force it. It's only just been attached. Your body will be accustomed to it in a few days. As I said earlier, you two were exceptionally compatible with each other. You should be able to recover enough even to resume normal life."

counterexamples.description: Compatibility applies to circuits only.
counterexamples.sourceReading: It does not make Heroic Spirit power safe for a human.
counterexamples.explanation: Compatibility applies to circuits only.

contexts.japanese: 「だが注意しろ。私が言っているのは、あくまで回路が合う、というだけの話だ。
contexts.english: "But be warned. I am only saying that your circuits were compatible.

counterexamples.description: A single use activates Archer's Magic Circuits.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The trigger is use, not gradual ordinary aging.
counterexamples.explanation: A single use activates Archer's Magic Circuits.

contexts.japanese: 「霊格として、衛宮士郎の肉体はアーチャーの腕には到底及ばん。一度でもその腕を使えば、アーチャーの魔術回路が起動する。
contexts.english: "Archer's arm is far beyond Shirou Emiya's spiritual core to sustain. If you use the arm even once, it will activate Archer's Magic Circuits.

counterexamples.description: Kirei rejects lifespan loss per use.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The correction is explicit.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei rejects lifespan loss per use.

contexts.japanese: いいか、使う度に寿命が減っていく、のではない。
contexts.english: Hear me—I am not saying that each use will shorten your life span.

counterexamples.description: Using the arm starts a time bomb.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The triggered countdown is distinct from baseline invasion.
counterexamples.explanation: Using the arm starts a time bomb.

contexts.japanese: その腕を使えば、おまえの体に植え付けられた時限爆弾にスイッチが入るのだ」
contexts.english: Once you use the arm, you will have lit the fuse on a time bomb."

counterexamples.description: Shirou understands one imitation as fatal.
counterexamples.sourceReading: This is his reading of the warning.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou understands one imitation as fatal.

contexts.japanese: 要するに一度でもアーチャーの真似事をすれば、俺は絶対に死ぬって事じゃないか。
contexts.english: Is he basically saying that if I try to copy what Archer does even once, I'm as good as dead?

counterexamples.description: The wrapping separates left-arm circuits from Shirou's spellcasting.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Magecraft elsewhere does not activate it as part of him.
counterexamples.explanation: The wrapping separates left-arm circuits from Shirou's spellcasting.

contexts.japanese: 「ああ、その為の封印だ。それを巻いているかぎり、左腕は魔術回路を発現しない。おまえが魔術を使おうと、その左腕だけは別の物として扱われる。
contexts.english: "Yes, they are a seal. So long as your left arm stays wrapped, its Magic Circuits will not manifest. Even if you use magecraft, the left arm won't act as a part of you.

counterexamples.description: The shroud suppresses invasion only to an extent.
counterexamples.sourceReading: It is not a complete cure.
counterexamples.explanation: The shroud suppresses invasion only to an extent.

contexts.japanese: その布を巻いている限り、左腕からの侵食はある程度抑えられる筈だ」
contexts.english: As long as the shroud stays on, it will hinder the arm's invasion of your body, to an extent."

counterexamples.description: The arm ultimately invades whether used or not.
counterexamples.sourceReading: This slow baseline danger differs from activation-triggered collapse.
counterexamples.explanation: The arm ultimately invades whether used or not.

contexts.japanese: 「抑えられん。……そうだな、アーチャーの腕を使おうと使うまいと、結局はその腕に侵食される。
contexts.english: That is impossible... I suppose whether you use Archer's arm or not, it will ultimately consume you.

counterexamples.description: Growth into a mage able to resist the arm is proposed as solution.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei's assessment remains prospective.
counterexamples.explanation: Growth into a mage able to resist the arm is proposed as solution.

contexts.japanese: 長生きがしたいのなら、腕と拮抗するほどの魔術師に成長しろ。そうなれば聖骸布を巻かずとも左腕の封印は出来る」
contexts.english: If you want to live longer, then grow into a mage that can resist the arm. Then you may be able to keep it sealed even without the aid of the shroud."

counterexamples.description: Kirei estimates ten years before consumption.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The duration is approximate and tied to his assessment.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei estimates ten years before consumption.

contexts.japanese: 「なに、私の見立てでは左腕に食い潰されるまでにあと十年。それだけの猶予があるのだ。一人前になって左腕を御するか、成れずに自滅するか。そう急な話ではあるまい」
contexts.english: "I give it about ten years until the arm devours you completely. That is how much time he bought you. You can become capable enough to control the arm on your own, or fail and die. Either way, it is hardly an urgent matter."

counterexamples.description: Unwrapping and using Archer's arm remains Shirou's choice.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei refuses to guarantee survival.
counterexamples.explanation: Unwrapping and using Archer's arm remains Shirou's choice.

contexts.japanese: 選択肢は常におまえにある。アーチャーの力を使うのは自由だが、使えば命の保証はせん。
contexts.english: The choice is always up to you. You're free to use Archer's arm, but I cannot guarantee your safety if you do.

counterexamples.description: Rin's toxin cleansing and Shirou's transplant are identified as completed treatments.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Completion does not erase future risk.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin's toxin cleansing and Shirou's transplant are identified as completed treatments.

contexts.japanese: チャーの左腕を移植され、凛は毒素を洗浄された。なにか、これ以上の要求はあるか？」
contexts.english: was transplanted to Shirou Emiya, and Rin has been detoxified. Do you have any further requests?"

counterexamples.description: Kirei predicts Zouken will retrieve or dispose of Sakura.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He says prevention is difficult and offers no duty/benefit.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei predicts Zouken will retrieve or dispose of Sakura.

contexts.japanese: 「間桐臓硯としては間桐桜を取り戻すか、始末するかのどちらかだろう。これを防ぐのは難しく、おまえたちには防ぐ義務もない。なにしろ間桐臓硯を倒したところで、おまえたちに益はないからな」
contexts.english: "Zouken Matou will likely decide to either retrieve Sakura Matou, or dispose of her. It would be difficult to prevent this, and neither of you are obligated to do so. After all, you have nothing to gain from defeating Zouken."

counterexamples.description: Rin explicitly refuses to forfeit.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She rejects Kirei's correct-choice framing.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin explicitly refuses to forfeit.

contexts.japanese: 「—ご忠告どうも。けど降りないわよ、わたし」
contexts.english: "...Thanks for the warning. But I'm not forfeiting."

counterexamples.description: Rin still identifies as a Master without a Servant.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She refuses an automatic withdrawal rule.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin still identifies as a Master without a Servant.

contexts.japanese: 「当然よ。サーヴァントがいなくなっても、わたしはまだマスターだもの。一人になったから戦いを降りるだろうなんて、勝手に極め付けないでよね」
contexts.english: "Of course not. I'm still a Master, even if I don't have a Servant. Don't go deciding on your own that I'll forfeit just because I'm alone."

counterexamples.description: Shirou also chooses to continue fighting Zouken.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He has a goal but no finished plan.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou also chooses to continue fighting Zouken.

contexts.japanese: 「ああ、戦いは止めない。俺だって目的はある。このまま臓硯の好きにはさせない」
contexts.english: "Yeah. I won't stop fighting. I have my own goal, too. I can't let Zouken do as he pleases."

counterexamples.description: Illya refuses Kirei and asserts control of her lodging.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The three parties reject his custody for their own reasons.
counterexamples.explanation: Illya refuses Kirei and asserts control of her lodging.

contexts.japanese: 「お断りするわ。わたし、自分の居場所は自分で決められるもの」
contexts.english: "No thanks. I'll decide where I'm going to stay."

counterexamples.description: Gilgamesh asks whether Kirei should let the Grail go.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The embodied Grail is leaving with the guests.
counterexamples.explanation: Gilgamesh asks whether Kirei should let the Grail go.

contexts.japanese: 「—いいのか、聖杯を逃がして」
contexts.english: "...Are you sure about letting the Holy Grail go?"

counterexamples.description: Kirei says he never had attachment to the Grail.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He will not stop it going with them.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei says he never had attachment to the Grail.

contexts.japanese: 「かまわん。初めから執着があった訳ではない。聖杯が彼らにつくのなら止めはしない」
contexts.english: "I don't mind. I was never fixated on it, to begin with. If the Grail goes to them, I won't stop it."

counterexamples.description: Kirei does not need the Grail's power.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The narration distinguishes need from inquiry.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei does not need the Grail's power.

contexts.japanese: 聖杯の力など、真実、言峰綺礼は必要としない。
contexts.english: In fact, Kirei Kotomine does not need the power of the Holy Grail.

counterexamples.description: Kirei is defined by relentless pursuit/inquiry.
counterexamples.sourceReading: This replaces ordinary wish as motive.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei is defined by relentless pursuit/inquiry.

contexts.japanese: 彼にあるのは、ただ徹底した“追究”のみ。
contexts.english: All he has is his earnest pursuit.

counterexamples.description: The wish machine returns only answers acceptable to the asker.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The epistemic circularity is explicit.
counterexamples.explanation: The wish machine returns only answers acceptable to the asker.

contexts.japanese: 自らに生じる疑問に、自らが良しとする答えしか生み出さない願望機だ。
contexts.english: It is a wish granter that can only give answers that one approves of, to questions that arise from oneself.

counterexamples.description: A desired answer is judged meaningless.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei seeks independence from his own wish.
counterexamples.explanation: A desired answer is judged meaningless.

contexts.japanese: そのような“自分が望んだ答え”になど、果たして何の意味があるのか。
contexts.english: And what meaning is there in an answer that one wished for?

counterexamples.description: Kirei frames both men's goals as pleasure pursuit, not personal wishes.
counterexamples.sourceReading: They act toward outcomes because the process/result is enjoyable.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei frames both men's goals as pleasure pursuit, not personal wishes.

contexts.japanese: 「願望機に用はない。それはおまえとて同じだろうギルガメッシュ。おまえの目的も私の目的も、その実自らの願いではない。単にそうした方が楽しいから、という快楽追求でしかない。
contexts.english: "I have no use for a granter of wishes. I'm sure that applies to you as well, Gilgamesh. Both of our goals are not wishes of our own. We simply pursue pleasure because we think the outcome would be amusing.

counterexamples.description: Kirei's name is presented as a prayer.
counterexamples.sourceReading: His father hopes for purity and beauty.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei's name is presented as a prayer.

contexts.japanese: 綺礼という名は祈りの言葉だという。
contexts.english: He was told that his name "Kirei" was a prayer.

counterexamples.description: Young Kirei possesses morals and precocious judgment.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He is not ignorant of right and wrong.
counterexamples.explanation: Young Kirei possesses morals and precocious judgment.

contexts.japanese: 子はその祈り通りに成長し、幼くして道徳と良識を持ち、早熟と思われるほど見識深かった。
contexts.english: The son grew up as his father hoped. From a young age, he was a surprisingly insightful youth who possessed good morals and wisdom.

counterexamples.description: Kirei understands his father's joy.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Understanding does not require reciprocal love.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei understands his father's joy.

contexts.japanese: 父は良い後継者に恵まれたと喜び、息子は父の喜びを理解していた。
contexts.english: His father was happy to have been blessed with a worthy successor, and the son understood his father's joy.

counterexamples.description: Kirei cannot understand what his father calls beautiful.
counterexamples.sourceReading: This is the single discrepancy amid healthy development.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei cannot understand what his father calls beautiful.

contexts.japanese: 父の言う“美しいもの”がなんであるか、それだけが理解できないと首を傾げながら。
contexts.english: He was always confused by what his father called "beautiful."

counterexamples.description: The moment of recognition has no known cause.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei himself cannot explain why then.
counterexamples.explanation: The moment of recognition has no known cause.

contexts.japanese: どうしてその時に判ってしまったのか、理由は定かではない。
contexts.english: He is not sure why he realized it at that moment.

counterexamples.description: He has never felt his father's beautiful things as beautiful.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The failure concerns felt valuation, not moral vocabulary.
counterexamples.explanation: He has never felt his father's beautiful things as beautiful.

contexts.japanese: それを—少年は、一度たりとも美しいと感じ得なかったのだから。
contexts.english: not once in his life had he ever felt the same about them.

counterexamples.description: Moth is preferred over butterfly.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The image begins a sequence of inverted attraction.
counterexamples.explanation: Moth is preferred over butterfly.

contexts.japanese: 彼が美しいと思うものは蝶ではなく蛾であり、
contexts.english: He thought moths were beautiful, not butterflies.

counterexamples.description: Evil, not good, attracts Kirei.
counterexamples.sourceReading: This coexists with moral belief.
counterexamples.explanation: Evil, not good, attracts Kirei.

contexts.japanese: 善ではなく悪だった。
contexts.english: Evil, not good.

counterexamples.description: Kirei understands goodness as right.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The problem is not inability to judge morality.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei understands goodness as right.

contexts.japanese: 人並みの良識を持ち、道徳を信じ、善である事が正しいと理解していながら。
contexts.english: Even though he had common sense, believed in morals, and understood that being good was just...

counterexamples.description: Kirei cannot tell whether his lack is suffering.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The narration qualifies the word rather than diagnosing him.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei cannot tell whether his lack is suffering.

contexts.japanese: 綺礼本人でさえ、それが苦悩であるかどうかさえ判断がつかなかった。
contexts.english: Even Kirei himself could not tell whether he was truly in anguish.

counterexamples.description: He seeks a capacity absent from the beginning.
counterexamples.sourceReading: His effort aims at purity and ordinary beauty.
counterexamples.explanation: He seeks a capacity absent from the beginning.

contexts.japanese: 清く美しくあれと、初めからなかった心を求め続けた。
contexts.english: He continued to seek purity and beauty, values that he never had from the beginning.

counterexamples.description: He searches the body for a place to receive what the heart lacks.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The self-punishment has a distorted but explicit rationale.
counterexamples.explanation: He searches the body for a place to receive what the heart lacks.

contexts.japanese: 心の中にないのなら、体のどこかに容れるべき個所がある筈だと探した事もある。
contexts.english: If he lacked it in his heart, then he might be able to find it elsewhere in his body.

counterexamples.description: The pilgrimage distance reaching the moon remains hyperbole.
counterexamples.sourceReading: It describes accumulated steps.
counterexamples.explanation: The pilgrimage distance reaching the moon remains hyperbole.

contexts.japanese: 刻んだ歩みで言うのなら、その距離は月にすら届くだろう。
contexts.english: He must have walked enough steps to reach the moon itself.

counterexamples.description: Spiritual penance is distinguished from physical suffering.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Believers value the former more.
counterexamples.explanation: Spiritual penance is distinguished from physical suffering.

contexts.japanese: 肉体的な苦痛を求めてではない。そも、信徒にとって重要なものは肉体的苦痛ではなく精神的苦行である。
contexts.english: He did not seek physical suffering. To begin with, believers like them valued spiritual penance over physical toil.

counterexamples.description: Kirei's morals demand punishment if he is born sinful.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The punishment seeks balance with the world.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei's morals demand punishment if he is born sinful.

contexts.japanese: 自分が生まれつきの罪人ならば、その程度の罰がなければ世界と釣りあわないと、彼が信じた道徳が教えたのだ。
contexts.english: According to the morals he was taught and believed in, if he was born a sinner, then it was only right that he suffer a fitting punishment.

counterexamples.description: Kirei lacks ordinary felt happiness.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The conclusion is not total emotional numbness.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei lacks ordinary felt happiness.

contexts.japanese: つまるところ、彼には生まれつき“人並みの幸福実感”がなかっただけだ。
contexts.english: In the end, he realized that he was born without the ability to feel what other humans called happiness.

counterexamples.description: Ordinary positive goods are enumerated.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Charity, trust, glory and security fail to give him joy.
counterexamples.explanation: Ordinary positive goods are enumerated.

contexts.japanese: 博愛、信頼、栄光、安全。
contexts.english: Charity. Trust. Glory. Security.

counterexamples.description: Others' suffering is the only delight named.
counterexamples.sourceReading: This is contrasted with strong morality.
counterexamples.explanation: Others' suffering is the only delight named.

contexts.japanese: 少年が“楽しい”と思える事は他人の苦しみでしかない。
contexts.english: He only found delight in the suffering of others.

counterexamples.description: Morality itself makes his disposition unhappy.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The conflict drives inquiry.
counterexamples.explanation: Morality itself makes his disposition unhappy.

contexts.japanese: ……彼にとっての不幸は、そんな思考回路でありながら十分すぎるほどの“道徳”を持っていた事だ。
contexts.english: ...What made him unhappy was the fact that he had such a strong sense of "morality" in spite of his thinking patterns.

counterexamples.description: Kirei tries to make himself ordinarily human and save himself.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He rejects merely indulging abnormal pleasure.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei tries to make himself ordinarily human and save himself.

contexts.japanese: 人並みの事柄で幸福を得られない自分を、人並みに戻し、どうにか救おうとしたのである。
contexts.english: he attempted to save himself by making himself more human.

counterexamples.description: Faith and priestly life are chosen as the path.
counterexamples.sourceReading: This is sincere attempted salvation.
counterexamples.explanation: Faith and priestly life are chosen as the path.

contexts.japanese: その道が信仰であり、父と同じく、神父として人生を説く事だった。
contexts.english: He walked a path of faith, and began to preach about life, like his father did.

counterexamples.description: He hopes divine forgiveness may include one born lacking.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The hope remains tentative.
counterexamples.explanation: He hopes divine forgiveness may include one born lacking.

contexts.japanese: ならば自分のような“生まれつき持ち得ぬ者”も救うのではないか、と考えた。
contexts.english: Then, perhaps even someone born with a fatal flaw would be saved as well.

counterexamples.description: Religious discipline never yields pleasure greater than others' suffering.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The negative attraction survives sincere observance.
counterexamples.explanation: Religious discipline never yields pleasure greater than others' suffering.

contexts.japanese: 神の教えを守り、規律に従い、質素に生きたものの、彼には“他者の苦しみ”に勝る悦びが見いだせなかった。
contexts.english: Even though he followed God's teachings, obeyed His laws, and lived a simple life, he never found any pleasure greater than the suffering of others.

counterexamples.description: He sought something he never possessed.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The next line says there was no loss to mourn.
counterexamples.explanation: He sought something he never possessed.

contexts.japanese: 初めから無いものを求めたのだ。
contexts.english: He was seeking something that he never had.

counterexamples.description: The enduring product is a question: why.
counterexamples.sourceReading: No salvation or resolution is achieved.
counterexamples.explanation: The enduring product is a question: why.

contexts.japanese: 成人し、神父となった男についてまわったものは、“なぜ”という疑問だけだ。
contexts.english: By the time the priest grew into a man, he was left with only one question: why?

counterexamples.description: Sin for affirmation would make sense to Kirei.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The hypothetical distinguishes chosen corruption from innate disposition.
counterexamples.explanation: Sin for affirmation would make sense to Kirei.

contexts.japanese: 罪を犯し、その背徳に酔うことで異常者である自身を肯定するというなら解る。
contexts.english: If a deviant like him felt affirmed by committing sin and getting drunk on corruption, that would make sense.

counterexamples.description: Vice for profit would also be logically intelligible.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Instrumental wrongdoing is contrasted with his case.
counterexamples.explanation: Vice for profit would also be logically intelligible.

contexts.japanese: 己が欲の為に他者を陥れ、その益によって更なる富を得ようというのなら道理が通る。
contexts.english: If he hurt others for his own greed and used that profit to reap further gain, that would be logically consistent.

counterexamples.description: Kirei asks about never possessing the good-to-evil choice.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Disposition precedes volition.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei asks about never possessing the good-to-evil choice.

contexts.japanese: 生まれつき、その“善から悪に変わる”という選択さえ持ち得ない、とはどういう事なのか。
contexts.english: Why did he never once face a choice to turn from good to evil?

counterexamples.description: He asks whether he was born broken and destined to harm.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The formulation remains a question.
counterexamples.explanation: He asks whether he was born broken and destined to harm.

contexts.japanese: それは壊れたもの、世界に害を成す事を前提として生まれるモノではないのか。
contexts.english: Did it mean that he was born broken and destined to inflict harm on the world?

counterexamples.description: An unwanted being is born despite the world's rejection of evil.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The argument concerns existence and responsibility.
counterexamples.explanation: An unwanted being is born despite the world's rejection of evil.

contexts.japanese: にも関わらず初めから“望まれないもの”が生み出され、
contexts.english: And yet, something that nobody wished was born, living a life

counterexamples.description: The unwanted being exists only for exclusion and death.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The bleak purpose claim remains within Kirei's argument.
counterexamples.explanation: The unwanted being exists only for exclusion and death.

contexts.japanese: ただ死ぬ為に、ただ疎まれる為だけに在るものがある。
contexts.english: that awaited only exclusion and death.

counterexamples.description: Blind faith yields no salvation.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The result is questioning and untargeted anger.
counterexamples.explanation: Blind faith yields no salvation.

contexts.japanese: 長い苦悩、盲目な信仰の果てに得たものは救いではない。
contexts.english: What he gained from his long anguish and blind faith was not salvation—

counterexamples.description: Gilgamesh asks why a wishless person became Master.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The framing dialogue returns from introspection.
counterexamples.explanation: Gilgamesh asks why a wishless person became Master.

contexts.japanese: 「では、何故マスターになどなった？　望みがないのであらば、聖杯など要らぬだろうに」
contexts.english: "Then why did you become a Master? If you have no desire, then you don't need the Holy Grail."

counterexamples.description: Kirei says the previous war centered on dislike of an opposite man.
counterexamples.sourceReading: No name is inserted here.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei says the previous war centered on dislike of an opposite man.

contexts.japanese: 「……無論だ。前回の聖杯戦争でさえ、私は聖杯にもその中身にも関心はなかった。あの時にあったものは、私と正反対の男に対する不快感だけだった」
contexts.english: "Of course. I was uninterested in its contents the last time, as well. I was only driven by my displeasure with a man who was my polar opposite."

counterexamples.description: The prospective being is human-created yet unwanted and called all the world's evil.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Birth remains in progress.
counterexamples.explanation: The prospective being is human-created yet unwanted and called all the world's evil.

contexts.japanese: “この世全ての悪”という、人々に生み出されながら、人々に望まれなかった何者か。
contexts.english: The thing called "all the evil in the world," created by the people yet unwanted by them.

counterexamples.description: The Grail cannot itself supply independent answers.
counterexamples.sourceReading: It realizes its holder's desires.
counterexamples.explanation: The Grail cannot itself supply independent answers.

contexts.japanese: 聖杯に答えは出せない。
contexts.english: There are no answers to be found in the Holy Grail.

counterexamples.description: Kirei distinguishes an answer-producing being from a wished answer.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The being's birth is hypothetical.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei distinguishes an answer-producing being from a wished answer.

contexts.japanese: 「答えを出すのではなく。答えを出せるモノを、聖杯から産み落とすとしたらどうなる」
contexts.english: "The Holy Grail will give me no answers. But what if it gives birth to something that can?"

counterexamples.description: The smile is compared to a dying woman's without naming her.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The youth is surprised by the expression.
counterexamples.explanation: The smile is compared to a dying woman's without naming her.

contexts.japanese: その笑みは死に逝く女が浮かべるものだ。
contexts.english: His smile is like that of a dying woman.

counterexamples.description: Kirei's eyes are not smiling.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The expression and gaze remain split.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei's eyes are not smiling.

contexts.japanese: 偶像を見上げる眼は笑ってはいない。
contexts.english: Looking up at the statue, the priest's eyes are not laughing.

counterexamples.description: Kirei vows to question even his Lord unto death.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The theological violence is figurative but forceful.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei vows to question even his Lord unto death.

contexts.japanese: この全霊を懸け、我が主さえ問い殺そう—」
contexts.english: I will question the Lord unto death, with all my might."

counterexamples.description: Shirou recalls Kirei's days-long prognosis.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He does not actually believe the lapse trivial.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou recalls Kirei's days-long prognosis.

contexts.japanese: 言峰は数日持たないと言った。
contexts.english: Kotomine said that she only has days left.

counterexamples.description: Saber recommends the church to learn about Einzbern.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She predicts Kirei can guide questions and course.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber recommends the church to learn about Einzbern.

contexts.japanese: 「……これも何かの因縁でしょう。アインツベルンを知りたいのなら、もう一度教会に赴くべきです。
contexts.english: "...This must be fated, somehow. If you wish to learn more of the Einzberns, then you should visit the church again.

counterexamples.description: Shirou recalls the rule limiting return to forfeiture.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He treats it as prohibition.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou recalls the rule limiting return to forfeiture.

contexts.english: "The church...? You mean the same one from yesterday? But I'm not supposed to go there anymore. The priest said only to come back if I'm going to forfeit being a Master."

counterexamples.explanation: Saber attributes the rule to Association policy regulating magi.

contexts.english: "That was just a white lie. The rules that priest enforces are a contrivance of the Mage's Association meant to control the battle between mages. Since you don't belong to the Association, there is no purpose in obeying them."

counterexamples.description: Shirou wants to avoid Kirei despite accepting the rule argument.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The hesitation is personal rather than legal.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou wants to avoid Kirei despite accepting the rule argument.

contexts.japanese: 「……そうだな。けど、それでも出来れば避けたい。……あの神父には、あんまり会わないほうがいい気がする」
contexts.english: "...I suppose you're right. But I still want to avoid it if I can. I have a feeling that I shouldn't see that priest any more than I have to."

counterexamples.description: Fear is not simple hostility, danger or distrust.
