counterexamples.explanation: Fear is not simple hostility, danger or distrust.

contexts.japanese: 危険だとか信用できないとか、そういう敵対意識からじゃない。
contexts.english: It isn't a feeling of hostility like I can't trust him or that he's a threat.

counterexamples.description: Repeated contact with Kirei feels capable of crumbling Shirou's self.
counterexamples.sourceReading: This is feared possibility, not completed corruption.
counterexamples.explanation: Repeated contact with Kirei feels capable of crumbling Shirou's self.

contexts.japanese: 会えば会うほど今まで築き上げてきた自分が崩れてしまいそうで、怖いのだ。
contexts.english: I'm afraid that the more I'm around him, the more of myself that I've built up over time will crumble away.

counterexamples.description: Saber shares the desire to avoid Kirei.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Her agreement surprises Shirou.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber shares the desire to avoid Kirei.

contexts.japanese: 「シロウの気持ちは分かる。私とて同感です。出来る事なら、あの神父には関わりたくない」
contexts.english: "I know how you feel, Shirou. I agree. We should avoid associating with him if possible."

counterexamples.description: Saber does not know which Servant Kirei commanded.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kiritsugu nonetheless treated him as major threat.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber does not know which Servant Kirei commanded.

contexts.japanese: どのサーヴァントのマスターだったかは判りませんが、切嗣はあの神父を最後まで重視していた」
contexts.english: I don't know which Servant he was the Master of, but Kiritsugu was cautious of him until the very end."

counterexamples.description: Kiritsugu saw Kirei as the only likely defeater.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The judgment remains Kiritsugu's.
counterexamples.explanation: Kiritsugu saw Kirei as the only likely defeater.

contexts.japanese: その中で—衛宮切嗣は、あの神父を最大の敵として捉えていました。私たちを破る者がいるとすれば、それはあの男以外ないと」
contexts.english: Kiritsugu judged that priest to be the greatest threat of all the participants. He said that if we lost, it would be to him."

counterexamples.description: Shirou asks why neither Kirei nor Kiritsugu told him.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The omissions drive his disbelief.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou asks why neither Kirei nor Kiritsugu told him.

contexts.japanese: 「—嘘だ。そんな事あるもんか。それならどうして言峰は黙ってたんだ。どうして切嗣は、俺に何も言わなかったんだ」
contexts.english: "...No way. How could it be? Why didn't Kotomine say anything? Why didn't the old man tell me?"

counterexamples.description: Saber's gaze urges Shirou to seek truth by his own will.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The movement to church is his choice.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber's gaze urges Shirou to seek truth by his own will.

contexts.japanese: 衛宮切嗣の真実を知りたければ、自分の意志で教会に向かえと、碧の瞳が告げていた。
contexts.english: if I want to know the truth about Kiritsugu Emiya, then I should willingly go to the church.

counterexamples.description: Saber waits outside and tells Shirou to face Kirei alone.
counterexamples.sourceReading: No abandonment is implied.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber waits outside and tells Shirou to face Kirei alone.

contexts.japanese: 「私はここで待機します。神父には貴方一人で向き合ってください」
contexts.english: "I will wait here. You should face the priest alone."

counterexamples.description: Saber warns Shirou to call her at danger.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei is described as ominous.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber warns Shirou to call her at danger.

contexts.japanese: 「……はい。シロウも注意を。危険が迫った時はすぐに私を呼んでください。あの神父はどこか不吉だ。少しでも気を抜けば、貴方の身に何が起こるか判らない」
contexts.english: "...Yes. Be careful, Shirou. If there is danger, call me immediately. There is something wicked about that priest. There is no telling what might happen if you let your guard down."

counterexamples.description: Shirou politely asks the stranger for Father Kotomine.
counterexamples.sourceReading: No recognition occurs.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou politely asks the stranger for Father Kotomine.

contexts.japanese: 「すみません。言峰神父はいらっしゃいますか」
contexts.english: "Excuse me. Is Father Kotomine here?"

counterexamples.description: The stranger tells Shirou to wait for Kirei.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He disappears behind altar.
counterexamples.explanation: The stranger tells Shirou to wait for Kirei.

contexts.japanese: 「そこで待っていろ。言峰に用があるのだろう」
contexts.english: "Wait there. You seek Kotomine, yes?"

counterexamples.description: Kirei mockingly asks whether Shirou retires after half a day.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The greeting frames their antagonistic banter.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei mockingly asks whether Shirou retires after half a day.

contexts.japanese: 「驚いたな。まさか半日たらずでリタイヤかね、衛宮士郎」
contexts.english: "I'm surprised. To think you'd retire after only half a day, Shirou Emiya."

counterexamples.description: Kirei replies that he does not want Shirou becoming attached/dependent.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He mirrors the hostility.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei replies that he does not want Shirou becoming attached/dependent.

contexts.japanese: 「それは結構。私も暇ではないのでね、簡単に懐かれても困る」
contexts.english: "That is fine with me. I'm a busy man as well, so I wouldn't want you becoming dependent."

counterexamples.description: Kirei's presence forces awareness of Shirou's weakness.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The severe atmosphere is both priestly asset and defect.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei's presence forces awareness of Shirou's weakness.

contexts.japanese: この男は、ただ立っているだけで己の弱さを意識させるような、厳格な雰囲気を持っている。
contexts.english: He gives off a severe air that makes me feel conscious of my flaws just by standing near him.

counterexamples.description: Kirei demands the question without pleasantries.
counterexamples.sourceReading: They are not friends.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei demands the question without pleasantries.

contexts.japanese: 「どうした？　質問があるのなら口にしろ。挨拶などする仲でもあるまい」
contexts.english: "And? State your question. We're hardly acquainted such that I feel a need to exchange pleasantries."

counterexamples.description: Shirou asks why Kirei concealed Kiritsugu's Master history.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The grievance is direct.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou asks why Kirei concealed Kiritsugu's Master history.

contexts.japanese: 「—切嗣の事だ。衛宮切嗣がマスターで、前回の聖杯戦争で戦ってたって事を、どうして黙っていた」
contexts.english: "About my old man. Why didn't you say that Kiritsugu Emiya was a Master in the last Holy Grail War?"

counterexamples.description: Kirei enjoys hearing Kiritsugu's name from Shirou.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He shows no shame.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei enjoys hearing Kiritsugu's name from Shirou.

contexts.japanese: ヤツに悪びれた様子はない。……この男は純粋に、俺の口から切嗣の名が出た事を楽しんでいる。
contexts.english: The priest doesn't show a hint of shame. In fact, he looks like he's enjoying hearing me say Kiritsugu's name.

counterexamples.description: Kirei argues Kiritsugu's deeds give Shirou no benefit.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The claim separates inherited fame from present ability.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei argues Kiritsugu's deeds give Shirou no benefit.

contexts.japanese: 「何故も何もなかろう。おまえの父が前回のマスターであった事が、おまえにとってなんの益になる。衛宮切嗣の功績は衛宮士郎には無関係だ」
contexts.english: "There was hardly any reason to. How would knowing that your father was a Master benefit you? Kiritsugu Emiya's deeds are irrelevant to Shirou Emiya."

counterexamples.description: Shirou argues Kiritsugu's history would have induced him to fight.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He treats omission as strategically surprising.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou argues Kiritsugu's history would have induced him to fight.

contexts.japanese: そんな説明より切嗣の事を言えば、俺はアンタの思い通り戦うと決めた筈だ。それを、どうして口にしなかった」
contexts.english: But if you had told me about Kiritsugu, then I would willingly fight in the war, just like you want. Why didn't you mention it?"

counterexamples.description: Kirei rejects known genetic succession because Shirou is not biological son.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He does not deny adoptive relation.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei rejects known genetic succession because Shirou is not biological son.

contexts.japanese: 遺伝によるマスターの継承など知らぬし、そもそもおまえは切嗣の息子ではあるまい。
contexts.english: I know of no genetic succession of Masterhood, and to begin with, you aren't Kiritsugu's blood-related son.

counterexamples.description: Shirou is exceptional because he lacked Grail knowledge and preparation.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei says he does not know why he was chosen.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou is exceptional because he lacked Grail knowledge and preparation.

contexts.japanese: 「本来、いかに魔術師であろうと聖杯を知らぬ者に令呪は宿らん。その例外であるおまえが選ばれた理由など、私の知るところではない」
contexts.english: "Normally, the Command Spells would not be bestowed upon someone who is ignorant of the Holy Grail, even if he is a mage. I don't know why an exception like you would occur."

counterexamples.description: Shirou seeks confirmation that rescue was pure goodwill.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The clause remains his formulation.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou seeks confirmation that rescue was pure goodwill.

contexts.japanese: ただ、純粋な善意で、死のうとしていた子供を助けただけだった、と。
contexts.english: ...sheer goodwill, because he wanted to save a dying child?

counterexamples.description: Kirei qualifies his answer as only what he knows.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He proposes Grail causation without certainty.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei qualifies his answer as only what he knows.

contexts.japanese: 「私が知る限りではな。だが聖杯の思惑となると、私には計り知れん。衛宮士郎がマスターに選ばれた事は偶然と切り捨てたいところだが、少なからず因果を感じる。
contexts.english: "As far as I know. But I cannot divine the will of the Holy Grail. As much as I'd like to dismiss your selection as random chance, I feel some karmic connection at work.

counterexamples.description: Kirei says Kiritsugu destroyed the Grail to end the war.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Betrayal is Kirei's personified framing.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei says Kiritsugu destroyed the Grail to end the war.

contexts.japanese: ヤツは最後の最後で聖杯を破壊した。聖杯戦争そのものを終わらせる為に、ヤツに期待を寄せた聖杯と、その宿願を裏切ったのだ」
contexts.english: In the last possible moment, he destroyed it. He turned on his own wish, on the grail's expectations, in order to end the Holy Grail War."

counterexamples.description: Shirou rejects betrayal and sees destruction as ending conflict.
counterexamples.sourceReading: This is his idealized judgment.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou rejects betrayal and sees destruction as ending conflict.

contexts.japanese: それを破壊した切嗣は、裏切ってなんかいない。
contexts.english: The old man didn't betray anything by destroying it.

counterexamples.description: Kirei offers the earlier Kiritsugu as correction.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He marks the story wasteful but pleasurable.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei offers the earlier Kiritsugu as correction.

contexts.japanese: —いいだろう。無駄な話だが、衛宮切嗣の正体を教えてやる」
contexts.english: ...Very well. Perhaps this is a waste of time, but I will tell you who that man truly was."

counterexamples.description: Kiritsugu sought a miracle beyond his own power.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The ideal is beyond human realization.
counterexamples.explanation: Kiritsugu sought a miracle beyond his own power.

contexts.japanese: 自身の力では叶わない奇跡。
contexts.english: He sought a miracle his own powers could not achieve.

counterexamples.description: The unknown route by which Kiritsugu entered the war remains conjectural.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei allows that an outside party may have noticed Kiritsugu's suitability and dismisses the detail.
counterexamples.explanation: The unknown route by which Kiritsugu entered the war remains conjectural.

contexts.japanese: 或いは、ヤツではない外部の者がヤツの適合性に目をつけたのかも知れん。そのあたりはどうでもいい話だ」
contexts.english: Perhaps another interested party saw potential in having him participate. It matters not."

counterexamples.description: Kiritsugu is retained as a hired Master.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He was employed as a Master rather than born into the participating family.
counterexamples.explanation: Kiritsugu is retained as a hired Master.

contexts.japanese: 「結論として、衛宮切嗣はマスターとして雇われた。
contexts.english: "Regardless, Kiritsugu Emiya was hired as a Master.

counterexamples.description: Einzbern combat weakness motivates recruiting Kiritsugu.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The family is ill suited to combat and entrusts hope to an unaffiliated killer skilled in killing contests.
counterexamples.explanation: Einzbern combat weakness motivates recruiting Kiritsugu.

contexts.japanese: 実際、アインツベルンの魔術は戦闘向きではない。彼らは戦いには不向きな一族だ。それ故に、殺し合いに長け、魔術協会に属さなかった切嗣に望みを託した」
contexts.english: In fact, the Einzbern mages themselves are not suited to fighting. Their clan is particularly ill-suited to it. Thus, they placed their hopes on Kiritsugu, a seasoned killer without ties to the Mage's Association."

counterexamples.description: Marriage, Master power and a combat-oriented heir remain distinct benefits.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Einzbern gives the heretic Grail knowledge and Master power and joins him to its bloodline to produce a more battle-ready successor.
counterexamples.explanation: Marriage, Master power and a combat-oriented heir remain distinct benefits.

contexts.japanese: 「異端である切嗣に聖杯の知識を与え、マスターとしての力を与え、アインツベルンの血と交わる事で、より戦闘向きの後継者を産み出しもした。
contexts.english: "They taught him—a heretic—knowledge of the Holy Grail, gave him the powers of a Master, and had him join with their bloodline in order to produce an even more battle-worthy heir.

counterexamples.description: The machine label remains Kirei's provisional characterization.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei first reduces Kiritsugu to a machine, then explicitly corrects literal emotionlessness on page68.
counterexamples.explanation: The machine label remains Kirei's provisional characterization.

contexts.japanese: 「一言で言ってしまえば、アレは機械だった。
contexts.english: "In a word, he was a machine.

counterexamples.description: Kiritsugu's weakness betraying everything is retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei says the weakness ultimately made him betray all invested hopes and his own wish.
counterexamples.explanation: Kiritsugu's weakness betraying everything is retained.

contexts.japanese: 「だが、そこまでして結局—その弱さが、ヤツに全てを裏切らせた。
contexts.english: "But in going to such extremes, his weakness betrayed everything he had:

counterexamples.description: Einzbern withdrawal and ten-year preparation remain chronological.
counterexamples.sourceReading: After Kiritsugu's betrayal the family retreats and spends ten years preparing the next Grail.
counterexamples.explanation: Einzbern withdrawal and ten-year preparation remain chronological.

contexts.japanese: 切嗣に裏切られたアインツベルンは撤退し、次の聖杯の用意に十年を費やした」
contexts.english: After Kiritsugu's treachery, the Einzberns retreated and have spent the last decade preparing for the next Holy Grail."

counterexamples.description: Kirei corrects caution to unavoidable attention.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He denies simple vigilance and says neither could fully ignore the other.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei corrects caution to unavoidable attention.

contexts.japanese: 「警戒ではない。互いに無視しても無視しきれぬ存在だっただけの話だ」
contexts.english: "I was not cautious of him. But I most certainly could not ignore him, either."

counterexamples.description: The one-for-ten sacrifice rule remains explicit.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kiritsugu personally and promptly sacrifices one when required to save ten.
counterexamples.explanation: The one-for-ten sacrifice rule remains explicit.

contexts.japanese: 人死にを許さぬくせに、人を助ける為に自らの手で人を殺す。十の命を生かす為に一の犠牲が必要とされるなら、速やかに自らの手で事を成した」
contexts.english: He could not abide death, yet he would kill others to save people. If a single life had to be sacrificed to save ten, then he would make that sacrifice without hesitation."

counterexamples.description: Kirei limits his claim about fidelity to what he knows.
counterexamples.sourceReading: As far as Kirei knows, Kiritsugu upheld his ideal until destroying the Grail.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei limits his claim about fidelity to what he knows.

contexts.japanese: 「ヤツは自らの理想に生きた。その理想は私の知りうる限り、聖杯を破壊するまで守られた筈だ。
contexts.english: "He chose to live for his ideals. As far as I am aware, he was faithful to them until the moment he destroyed the Holy Grail.

counterexamples.description: Kirei's deliberately provocative Anti-Hero gloss survives.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He first gives the literal opposite-of-hero framing and calls it an incorrigible killer.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei's deliberately provocative Anti-Hero gloss survives.

contexts.japanese: 「字の如しだが？　英雄の反対、度し難い殺人者という意味だ」
contexts.english: "Does the word not explain itself? It is the opposite of a hero: an incorrigible killer."

counterexamples.description: Kirei's mixed reaction to reliance by his enemy's son remains comic and unsettled.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He welcomes Shirou yet cannot settle whether to rejoice or grieve at being relied upon by Kiritsugu's son.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei's mixed reaction to reliance by his enemy's son remains comic and unsettled.

contexts.japanese: 「なんと。誤解があるようだが、私はおまえを歓迎しているぞ？　なにしろ切嗣の息子だ。仇敵の息子に頼りにされてみろ。喜ぶべきか悲しむべきか、複雑すぎて心が定まらん」
contexts.english: "Perish the thought. Lest you misunderstand, I welcome you. You are his son, after all. The child of my nemesis is coming to me for help. Should I rejoice or lament? My feelings are so mixed I can hardly bear it."

counterexamples.description: The sacrificed villain thought experiment retains its moral inversion.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Even a thoroughly evil man becomes a hero if sacrificing him saves the village.
counterexamples.explanation: The sacrificed villain thought experiment retains its moral inversion.

contexts.japanese: 「たとえ極悪人であろうと、その人間を生贄にする事で村人全員が助かるのなら、それは間違いなく英雄だろう？
contexts.english: "Imagine the most vile man you can think of. If his sacrifice would save everybody else in a village, would that not make him a hero?

counterexamples.description: Peace and Anti-Heroes remain parallel impossible wishes.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei instructs Shirou to remember the Anti-Hero as one unfulfillable wish treated as synonymous with peace.
counterexamples.explanation: Peace and Anti-Heroes remain parallel impossible wishes.

contexts.japanese: 平穏と同義とされる、叶う事のない願いの一つが、反英雄と呼ばれるモノと覚えておけばいい」
contexts.english: Just know that Anti-Heroes are a wish that can never be granted, treated much the same as peace itself."

counterexamples.description: Shirou rejects heroism as a wish-granted office.
counterexamples.sourceReading: A hero is what one has become after events are over, not something one sets out to become; the Grail supplies disproportionate power.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou rejects heroism as a wish-granted office.

contexts.japanese: 「そ、そんなの知るかっ！　とにかく違うものは違うんだ。それにな、英雄なんてのはなるものじゃなくて、終わった後になってるもんだろ。聖杯が用意できるものなんて、結局分不相応の力だけじゃないのか」
contexts.english: "I-I don't know! But I know they're different. Plus, a hero isn't something you try to be, but someone you become after everything's over. All the Holy Grail can do is give you power beyond your means, right?"

counterexamples.description: Shirou notices that Kirei has never belittled Kiritsugu.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Despite saying many hostile things, Kirei has not once spoken slightingly of him.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou notices that Kirei has never belittled Kiritsugu.

contexts.japanese: 色々言ってるけど、切嗣を一度もけなしていない。
contexts.english: He's said a lot of stuff about Kiritsugu, but none of it belittled him.

counterexamples.explanation: The conflict-free world remains impossible on earth.

contexts.english: A world without conflict does not exist on this earth. He sought out the Holy Grail because he could not abide that fact."

counterexamples.explanation: Kiritsugu's dream remains impossible even through the impossible Grail.

contexts.japanese: 衛宮切嗣という男の夢は、聖杯という“あり得ないもの”でしか叶わない、叶う筈のない魔法だった」
contexts.english: The dream of Kiritsugu Emiya was an impossible, magical idea that only an impossible device like the Holy Grail could make come true."

counterexamples.description: Universal desire for a world without conflict or suffering remains Kirei's assent.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei agrees that such a world is what everyone seeks.
counterexamples.explanation: Universal desire for a world without conflict or suffering remains Kirei's assent.

contexts.japanese: 争いのない世界、苦しみのない世界こそが万人の求めるものだと。
contexts.english: affirming that a world without conflict or suffering is something that all people want.

counterexamples.description: Wish is defined as the person's most comfortable state of being.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei says wishes express what feels most comfortable, with Kiritsugu's standard being a conflict-free world and Kirei's different from the outset.
